flags.detail: 'Anyons not fermions' and the SL(2,C)=Spin(3,1) bosonic/spinorial dictionary rest on a Sym-parity type-match (even Sym block = integer spin = tensorial/bosonic under SL(2,C)); the arc itself flags this is not a physics claim, but the type-coincidence is exactly what licenses the later child-program's spin-statistics framing throughout B429/B430.

'the chirality field (B147/B316/B444) — its THIRD independent appearance' at period 4 rests on discriminant -7 recurring across different constructions; the arc itself flags the promiscuity risk via the silver control (small discriminants recur), which is good practice, but the naming ('the chirality field') still asserts a shared identity across three different computational mechanisms based on matching discriminant value.

'disc(trace) x disc(Alexander)' is reinterpreted post hoc as 'disc(geometry) x disc(dynamics)' once the fig-8 case is shown to work, generalized to a 'conductor law' from exactly two confirmed data points (golden, silver) plus one registered-but-unrun bronze prediction; the pattern-fit is elegant but the inductive base is thin (n=2).

the arc explicitly and repeatedly flags 'ℤ/2×ℤ/2 ≅ C×P' as a structural predicate that cannot fire H1 alone and is HELD per standing rules -- this is good discipline, but the underlying observation (Klein-four Galois group of a biquadratic field matching the abstract group structure of C, P) is exactly the kind of bit/type coincidence this seat is instructed to flag regardless of how it's disposed of.

F1's whole design is an explicit attempt to guard against a bit-vs-value dimension-coincidence identification (metallic eigenvalue ratios 'looking like' CKM mixing parameters, the classic B428-lineage trap); the arc's own discipline (fixed function class, null model, HELD naming rule) is the correct response and the scan comes back null, so the identification-by-type temptation is explicitly tested and rejected rather than asserted.

The refuted claim itself ('span 36 = gl(2) x gl(3) = SM gauge algebra') is flagged in-arc as exactly this type of trap; correctly caught and refuted by the arc's own authors, but recorded here per the seat's licence-to-ask duty.
